Kiln & Quire, a letterpress and risograph print shop in Kyoto

Kiln

A weekend at the press

Two days, six people, and an edition of twenty prints you made yourself. No experience needed. Bring a word, a drawing, or nothing at all.

Kyoto
1/20 Kiln & Quire

Saturday, 10:00

Set it in metal

Choose from our cases of wood and lead type, Japanese and Latin, and set a word or a short line by hand, one letter at a time. Type is set as a mirror image, so it reads backwards until it meets paper.

Saturday, 14:00

Pull the first proof

Lock the forme into our 1964 platen press, ink the rollers, and pull. The first sheet off the press is the moment everything turns the right way round. You print the whole run of twenty before tea.

Sunday, 10:00

Overprint it on the risograph

Cut or draw a second colour, burn it onto a master, and feed your letterpress sheets back through the riso in fluorescent pink. Where pink crosses blue, a violet appears that neither ink has on its own.

Sunday, 16:00

Take home twenty

Your edition is trimmed, numbered, signed and wrapped flat for the flight home.

When
Every weekend, October to March
Group
Six people, taught in English and Japanese
Cost
¥32,000, including paper, ink and lunch
